correctness.rationale: For each integer h≥2 and character of order infinity or q>2h, Haar orthogonality is exact through degree 2h. Triangle inequalities reduce to nonnegative coefficients; a constant-term walk expansion strictly balances the endpoint magnitudes. The normalized moment P_h(x)/(1+x)^h has derivative Q_h/(1+x)^(h+1); Q_h coefficient signs vary exactly once, with positive constant and negative leading coefficient, so it has one simple positive maximizer. The z² convolution coefficient enforces the exact phase condition. For finite q≤2h, strictly positive coefficients at degrees 0 and q alias, proving strict excess. The uniform one-dimensional Laplace expansion, its derivative, and the unique L-infinity maximizer give x_h=2−3/(2h)+O(h^-2) and C_h=3^h sqrt(3/(8πh))(1+O(1/h)). The extracted checker verifies h=2..15 identities and finite grids, plus selected large-h drift; experiments are corroborative only.
